title: Boss Simulator
description: The usual arrangement, inverted: you are the boss, and the computer is the one dodging. A target hovers inside a lit arena and tries very hard to stay alive; you have nine attacks along the bottom and sixty seconds to take a thousand points off it. What makes it a game rather than a button-masher is that the target is genuinely good at this — every frame it scores sixteen directions for danger, including where each projectile in flight will be fifteen frames from now, and walks down the steepest gradient it finds — and that mashing does not pay. Attacks cost energy from one shared pool, each attack can only land once every sixth of a second, and a target that is still free to move is GUARDED and takes half damage. Only while it is pinned does it take triple. So the game is the sentence the original was always about: close the exits, pin it, then spend everything. Squeeze the arena with the crusher until there is only a corridor left, put a freeze into that corridor, and empty the pool into the second and a half you bought. Drawn in three.js through a tilted camera, so the walls have height, the target casts a shadow, and the crusher's slabs really do close in.
